# moz_task local MyFuture behavior chain

Source: Firefox `1a097ed8d31f6b307a5d0ebc34a82ceaf7f3727b`. Companion Thunderbird revision: `87d0159c7149a43253964c2cb6917939557dc799`.

Frozen target calls the example YieldingFuture. Actual pinned source calls it MyFuture; behavior and branch are unchanged.

This record covers the selected local future branch. It reuses 16 existing body records and reads missing imported, native, ownership, and generated-binding contracts. It does not close every moz_task function or caller.

## trigger and test contract

RustMozTask.Future calls the exported Rust_Future with a false flag. The selected branch constructs MyFuture(true), spawns it locally, awaits the join, and asserts 6. MyFuture asserts the expected main-thread condition each poll. This is the actual symbol; YieldingFuture in the frozen target was a mistaken label for this same behavior.

## entry and owner creation

The public spawn_local creates a TaskBuilder. TaskBuilder::spawn_local obtains the current nsIThread, panics if acquisition fails, retains that target in an Arc-owned TaskSpawnConfig, moves the future into async_task::spawn_local, schedules the initial runnable, and wraps the Task as a fallible join.

## actual imported implementation

moz_task requests async-task 4.3; the workspace lockfile and vendored crate identify 4.3.0. Its spawn_local wraps the future in Checked, which checks the spawning Rust thread ID before polling and before dropping the inner future. spawn_unchecked allocates a shared task header, schedule closure, and future with initial SCHEDULED, TASK, and REFERENCE state, returning distinct Runnable and Task handles.

## schedule and dispatch flags

Runnable::schedule transfers its handle to the stored schedule callback. moz_task::schedule captures the runnable in a one-shot RunnableFunction and retains another config Arc. It sets AT_END only while this task is currently polled on this thread. It sets FALLIBLE when the target is the current thread. Initial dispatch has no AT_END; self-wake rescheduling from run has AT_END. This target handles normal priority; AT_END is a hint and does not make this task idle.

## native queue routing

nsThread::DispatchFromScript adds a reference and calls nsThread::Dispatch, which forwards to its ThreadEventTarget. That target retains the runnable until PutEvent succeeds or its failure policy releases/leaks it. ThreadEventQueue checks runnable priority and rejects a doomed queue before transferring the event. Main-thread initialization selects an EventQueue that forwards to TaskController. Normal priority selects no idle manager, so DispatchRunnable creates a MainThreadOnly RunnableTask with the original runnable.

## native consumption

TaskController retains the MainThreadOnly task in its task set. The main-thread event loop obtains TaskController processing runnables. Those call ProcessPendingMTTask, which selects and runs a main-thread task. RunnableTask::Run calls the stored nsIRunnable::Run, clears its owning reference, and returns Complete; the controller marks the task complete and releases current-task ownership. The Rust RunnableFunction takes its callback from the Option before calling it; that callback sets POLLING_TASK and calls async_task::Runnable::run.

## poll, self-wake, and retry

RawTask::run changes SCHEDULED to RUNNING and polls the inner future. MyFuture increments poll_count and stores a cloned task waker. On counts 1 through 5 it wakes by reference and returns Pending. RawTask::wake_by_ref marks a running task SCHEDULED without dispatching immediately. The Pending branch sees SCHEDULED, calls schedule, and returns true. moz_task ignores that Boolean because the callback already queued the next run. On count 6 MyFuture returns Ready(6) without another wake.

## completion and join consumer

The Ready branch drops the completed future, writes its output, sets COMPLETED, removes runnable ownership, and wakes the registered awaiting task. Task::poll_task registers the outer waker while incomplete; once completed it marks CLOSED and moves the stored output into Ready(Some(6)). FallibleTask forwards that result. moz_task AsyncTask::poll unwraps Some into Ready(6), allowing the selected Rust assertion to compare the result to 6.

## ownership on completion

The task owns the Checked future and schedule closure. Checked drops MyFuture on its spawning thread; dropping MyFuture also drops its stored Waker. Waker drop and runnable completion remove counted references. After the awaited Task handle is dropped, Task::drop calls set_canceled (a no-op for an already completed/closed task) and set_detached, which clears TASK and destroys the allocation when no counted references remain. destroy drops the schedule closure, releasing its config Arc and retained XPCOM target, then deallocates the task. Additional live wakers would delay allocation release; this MyFuture stores its only explicit cloned waker inside the future that completion drops.

## native wrapper ownership

The generated XPCOM allocate function puts RunnableFunction in a Box and returns an owning RefPtr; native dispatch adds its own reference. The generator releases the Box when its reference count reaches zero. On execution, taking the callback removes its captured runnable/config before the native wrapper is released. On dispatch rejection, the fallible native wrapper allows normal RefPtr release, so the uncalled closure drops its Runnable and cancels/drops the pending future on the correct thread.

## errors and cancellation

A failure to get the thread panics. Dispatch rejection is logged by schedule; it is not returned as a Result from the join. On a canceled runnable, FallibleTask eventually returns None, which moz_task AsyncTask maps to Pending, so ordinary awaiting never completes with a cancellation result. Dropping AsyncTask drops its contained Task and cancels it; explicit AsyncTask::cancel awaits Option<T> and returns Some only if the task completed first. Task cancellation schedules a stopped task once to drop its future. A panic during poll runs the raw guard to close/drop the future if Rust unwinding occurs; destructor panics abort. Build-specific panic/FFI behavior was not executed and this record promises no recovery from panic.

impl<T> Future for AsyncTask<T> {
    type Output = T;

    fn poll(mut self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<Self::Output> {
        // Wrap the future produced by `AsyncTask` to never resolve if the
        // Runnable was dropped, and the task was cancelled.
        match Pin::new(&mut self.task).poll(cx) {
            Poll::Ready(Some(t)) => Poll::Ready(t),
            Poll::Ready(None) | Poll::Pending => Poll::Pending,
        }
    }
}
